explanation: Fall-through without break causes execution to continue to the next case; outputs A then B.
continue skips the rest of the iteration when i == 1, so only 0 and 2 are printed.
do-while executes at least once before checking the condition; 0 is printed, then x < 0 is false.
foreach iteration variable is a copy for value types; modifying x doesn't change the array.
finally block always executes after try or catch, overwriting x before the method returns.
break exits the loop when i == 3, so only 0, 1, 2 are printed.
Nested if: x > 3 is true, x < 10 is true, so A is printed, then C is always printed.
Loop adds 0 + 1 + 2 = 3, but sum starts at 0, so after accumulation sum = 3 (wait, let me recalculate: sum = 0 + 0 + 1 + 2 = 3).
Switch expression (C# 8+) matches x == 2 and returns 20.
while loop runs as long as i < 3; prints 0, 1, 2 then exits when i becomes 3.
